doc.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Thelonious Monk's indispensable repertory
summary: Tolliver calls Monk both harmonic foundation and musical theater, recalls talking with him, and says young players must know his music.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Well let’s not forget Thelonious Monk. That’s a whole ‘nother category by itself. Because not only was he the underpinnings harmonically for modern jazz, but he was musical theater at the same time. I mean you couldn’t make him up, you can’t make that up you know, because I got a chance to actually be close enough to see — you know, actually to talk to him. But talking to him was like talking to a psychiatrist who didn’t answer you back. You know. Yes. So the Thelonious Monk repertory is like Horace Silver. I mean it’s like, you know, it’s indispensable. It’s a requirement. If you haven’t dealt with that then you’re missing on some validity you know. Now nobody may not tell any young fellow or anything like that, they have to already, it’s just, they have to already have mother wit. You know what mother wit is? Mother wit, you have to already have it, to do that on your own, so that you don’t have to copy it, you have to know it though. You have to know it.
